entries.text: The Lagna (ascendant) and its lord describe the body, temperament, vitality and the overall direction of life; the strength and placement of the Lagna lord is a first measure of the native's resilience.
The Moon signifies the mind and emotions. Its sign, nakshatra and the planets aspecting or joining it colour the native's mental disposition and receptivity.
A benefic in a kendra (1,4,7,10) or trikona (1,5,9) tends to protect and uplift the houses it influences; a malefic there can add force, ambition or friction depending on its dignity.
The 10th house and its lord, together with the Sun, Saturn and Mercury, indicate profession, status and one's public role; the Dasamsa (D10) refines the reading of career.
Wealth is read from the 2nd (accumulated resources) and 11th (gains and fulfilment of desires) houses and their lords, with Jupiter and Venus as natural significators of prosperity.
Marriage and partnership are judged from the 7th house and its lord, from Venus, and — for depth — from the Navamsa (D9) and the Upapada Lagna (UL).
The 6th, 8th and 12th are the dusthana (difficult) houses; planets there often work through challenge, service, transformation or loss, and their results ripen especially in their dashas.
A retrograde planet is considered strong in motion (cheshta bala) but internalised in expression; a combust planet near the Sun loses visibility and independent effect.
A planet in its own sign or exaltation gives its results readily and auspiciously; in debilitation or an enemy's sign it must struggle to deliver, though neecha-bhanga (cancellation) can restore it.

The Vimsottari dasha sequences the unfolding of results in time: the maha-dasha lord sets the theme of the period and the bhukti (sub-period) lord modifies it, read through the houses each lord rules and occupies.

Gochara (transit) results are judged from the natal Moon: certain houses from the Moon are favourable for each planet, but a favourable transit can be cancelled by vedha (an obstructing planet in a specific house).

Sade Sati, Saturn's roughly seven-and-a-half year transit over the 12th, 1st and 2nd from the natal Moon, is a period of maturation and responsibility rather than mere misfortune; its effect depends on Saturn's natal dignity and the houses it rules.
The 9th house, its lord and Jupiter indicate dharma, fortune, higher learning and the guiding values of life; a strong 9th supports grace, ethics and good counsel.
Raja yogas form when lords of kendras and trikonas associate; they indicate rises in status and authority, timed to the dashas of the planets involved.
The Arudha Lagna (AL) shows how the native is perceived by the world — image, reputation and material manifestation — as distinct from the Lagna, which shows the actual self.
